Use Tier 2: replace independent positive/negative BCE with sampled-softmax cross-entropy, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. The supplied experiments reached 0.4175 with candidate-conditioned attention and 0.4012 after restoring SASRec, so changing the encoder alone did not recover the 0.505 baseline. BCE treats candidate scores independently, whereas evaluation measures the positive item’s rank against competing candidates. A competitive objective is therefore a specific hypothesis for improvement; the results do not establish that the loss caused the gap.

Keep the current encoder, initialization, prefix sampler, 32 uniform training negatives, optimizer, and training schedule unchanged to isolate the objective change. For each training prefix, compute the existing model’s 33 candidate logits and apply cross-entropy with candidate index zero as the positive class, replacing both BCE terms without adding auxiliary losses or score corrections. This directly trains the positive score to exceed competing negative scores while preserving the existing model’s inference interface. Select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 with 200 users, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42, and treat the pinned host macro-average as authoritative. Preserve all four category routes, supplied splits, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts; the predictor must load exactly one trained checkpoint per category and use identical history processing during validation and held-out inference. Keep execution single-GPU within the remaining shared budget, print the measured Final Validation Score, and leave hidden-test evaluation to the host without accessing test files or generating a speculative submission.
